subject: Prorated minimums & embedded-context billing — Opsly invoice question
raw_messages:
From: Amara Singh <amara@opsly.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@opsly.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice Q3 — need help mapping charges to usage

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our finance team pushed back on the Q3 invoice and asked for a clear mapping of the line items back to our runtime patterns. Two quick questions they couldn't reconcile:

1) Prorated minimums: the invoice shows three "minimum" line items for July/Aug/Sept. We have a mix of short streaming calls (bot interactions) and batch embeddings jobs. How are minimums prorated when a single account uses both streaming and batch calls in the same month? Are minimums applied per-call-type or per-account?

2) Embedded-context token accounting: a portion of our app stores short embedded contexts with each user query (roughly 450 tokens of stored context that are stitched at call-time). On the invoice these sometimes appear as separate calls and sometimes get bundled. What rules decide when embedded context counts as a new billable context vs appended to the caller's session?

I've attached the Opsly sample invoice and a small CSV export of calls. Any chance you can give an annotated example (2–3 concrete calculations) so our AP team can reconcile?

Appreciate it — Amara

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Amara Singh <amara@opsly.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prorated minimums & embedded-context billing — Opsly invoice question

Hi Amara — thanks for the note and the files. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Jonas (finance) to provide line-by-line examples.

Quick summary up front:
- Minimums are applied at the subscription (account) level and are not split by call-type. We do, however, apply different bucketization rules when calls are dominated by streaming vs batch for the purposes of rounding (see Ben's note).
- Embedded-context is billed as part of the request token count when it is stitched server-side at call time. Whether it gets "bundled" on the invoice depends on the aggregation window (billing quantum) and whether calls reuse an active conversation context.

Ben and Jonas — Opsly included an export that mixes many short interactive sessions with periodic bulk embedding runs. Can you attach two short worked examples (one short-session + embedded context, one batch embedding run) showing raw tokens, rounding, and final billed units?

I'll follow up after we have the worked examples with a short note you can share with Opsly AP.

— Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Amara Singh <amara@opsly.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prorated minimums & embedded-context billing — Opsly invoice question

Hi all — ran the numbers against the CSV. Two worked examples below (I attached a spreadsheet with line-by-line math). I kept the math intentionally conservative to match the invoice rounding.

Policy / constants used (for Opsly invoice period):
- Billing quantum: 100-token units. All per-request token counts are rounded up to the next 100-token quantum.
- Account minimum: 10,000 tokens / month (applies at account level). If total billed tokens (post-rounding) < minimum, we invoice the minimum; otherwise we invoice actual usage.
- Context-window bundling: requests that occur within an active conversation window (30 minutes of activity) share an "active context" and are aggregated for the purpose of contextual token bundling. Standalone batch jobs are isolated.
- Embedded-context handling: server-side stitched stored context tokens are counted in the request token total. If the same stored context is reused within the same active context window, we only bill the context tokens once per window (we still bill request tokens each call).

Example A — interactive support bot (sept-04)
- 7 calls from a single user over 22 minutes. Each call includes 450 tokens of stored context + user prompt ~ 60 tokens + model response ~ 120 tokens.
- Raw per-call token totals: 630 tokens. Round each to 700 (next 100). Per-call billed units: 7 units (700/100).
- Naive per-call billed tokens: 7 * 700 = 4,900 billed tokens.
- Active-context bundling rule: stored context (450 tokens) reused across the 22-minute window — bill stored context once for the whole window, not per call.
- Adjusted billing: stored context billed once = 500 tokens (rounded up), plus 7 * (user+response tokens rounded) = 7 * 200 = 1,400. Total billed tokens = 1,900.
- Result: because of bundling, Opsly sees 1,900 billed tokens for that 7-call interaction instead of 4,900.

Example B — batch embedding job (sept-05)
- One batch job processes 2,350 short documents; average per-document tokens to embed = 180 tokens.
- Per-document rounded unit: 200 tokens (next 100). Per-document billed tokens = 200 * 2,350 = 470,000 billed tokens.
- No active conversation window applies; batch is isolated and billed per-call-document.

Minimum check (account level)
- Sum all billed tokens for month after rounding and bundling. If total < 10,000, invoice shows account minimum of 10,000. For Opsly's Q3 invoice the three minimums were applied because Opsly had two months where the post-bundling total for the account fell below the monthly minimum threshold (July and August). September shows usage above minimum so actual usage billed.

Notes / caveats
- You can request a call to review the CSV with us on screen. If Opsly expects sustained low-interactive volumes we can propose a reduced minimum for a pilot term (requires PO and an amendment to the subscription).
- We bill streaming calls in the same quantum; the only difference is that short streaming heartbeats (keeps alive pings < 10 tokens) are deduped within the 30 minute active window and not billed repeatedly.

I'll paste the small worked math into Opsly-friendly language in my next message; attaching the spreadsheet now.

— Ben
